resolutions.finding: C1. R051 presents passesProseThrough prose-pass-through as shipped; R052 says markdownBlockSelection defaults true. One must be wrong.
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT. MarkdownBlockSelectionKey.defaultValue is `true` (MarkdownView.swift:856-858). A whole-repo grep for `markdownBlockSelection` returns exactly three sites and all three are READS: LinkParagraphView.swift:30 (makeNSView), LinkParagraphView.swift:37 (updateNSView), MarkdownView.swift:889 (@Environment in the MarkdownBlockSelection ViewModifier). There is no `.environment(\.markdownBlockSelection, ...)` anywhere in the checkout; a repo-wide grep for `.environment(\.` returns zero hits at all. Therefore the value is always true. LinkParagraphView.swift:30 and :37 both compute `view.passesProseThrough = !context.environment.markdownBlockSelection`, so passesProseThrough is always false (it also defaults false at LinkParagraphView.swift:285). LinkTextView.hitTest is `override func hitTest(_ point: NSPoint) -> NSView? { guard passesProseThrough, let superview else { return super.hitTest(point) } ... }` (LinkParagraphView.swift:436-442): the guard fails on the first clause on every call, so lines 439-441 (the local-coordinate convert, the linkAndRange/headMention test, and `return nil`) never execute. ProseRunRepresentable does not read the environment at all: it hardcodes `view.passesProseThrough = false` (ProseRunView.swift:86). R051 is wrong to state the prose-pass-through as shipped behavior; R052 is right about the default but stops before drawing the consequence. Corollary: in the MarkdownBlockSelection ViewModifier (MarkdownView.swift:888-897) the `if enabled` branch (line 892, `.textSelection(.enabled)`) always runs and the else branch (line 894, `.textSelection(.disabled)`) is dead.
resolutions.port_impact: SOURCE FACT + ENGINEERING DECISION. The port implements one behavior only: an AppKit-equivalent text surface that always takes its own hit test (the Windows equivalent of `super.hitTest`), shows a pointing-hand cursor over links and an I-beam over prose, and never passes prose clicks through to a whole-reply selection layer. Per-block text selection is always ON. Do NOT implement a whole-reply drag-selection mode; whole-reply copy goes through the row menu's `Copy message` / `Copy as markdown` items (TimelineRows.swift:219-220). The port may keep a disabled flag mirroring markdownBlockSelection for structural fidelity, but it must default to true and have no writer.

resolutions.finding: C2. R052 (MarkdownView) leaves markdownProseRuns undetermined; R052 (ProseRunView) asserts it conditionally. Neither states the settled consequence.
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT. MarkdownProseRunsKey.defaultValue is `true` (MarkdownView.swift:860-862). Grep finds exactly two references to `markdownProseRuns`: the EnvironmentValues accessor (MarkdownView.swift:881-884) and the read `@Environment(\.markdownProseRuns) private var proseRuns` (MarkdownView.swift:17). The only use of `proseRuns` is MarkdownView.swift:71: `if !isStreaming && proseRuns {`. It is never written, so the condition reduces to `if !isStreaming`. Consequence, settled: a FINISHED reply always takes the ProseRunView branch (MarkdownView.swift:71-86) - `VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 12)` over `MarkdownView.segments(blocks)`, with `.prose(run)` rendering `ProseRunView(blocks: run)` and `.block(block)` rendering `MarkdownBlockView(block:).equatable().transition(Self.transition(for: block))`. A STREAMING reply always takes the else branch (MarkdownView.swift:87-100) - the per-block `MarkdownBlockView(block:settled:)` stack with `.environment(\.markdownStreaming, isStreaming && index == last)`. `MarkdownView.segments` (MarkdownView.swift:25-44) groups `.heading/.paragraph/.list/.quote` into a prose run and breaks the run at `.code/.table/.rule`, which each become their own `.block`. So code blocks, tables and rules still go through MarkdownBlockView in a finished reply; only heading/paragraph/list/quote switch renderer. Also note that in the ProseRunView branch `.environment(\.markdownVeiled, isStreaming)` (MarkdownView.swift:84) is necessarily false, since the branch requires !isStreaming.
resolutions.port_impact: SOURCE FACT. The port must implement BOTH renderers and switch on isStreaming alone. Finished prose = the single-text-surface renderer (ProseRunView semantics). Streaming prose = the per-block view stack. Code/table/rule always use the block renderer. No user-facing setting controls this.

resolutions.finding: C3. R012 describes the row-expansion reveal as one mechanism; R010 documents TimelineRevealBox as two closures.
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT. `TimelineRevealBox` (ThreadTimeline.swift:2207-2221) is a `@MainActor final class ... Equatable` (identity equality, `lhs === rhs`) with two stored closures, both defaulting to `{}`: `var action: () -> Void` (:2208) and `var follow: () -> Void` (:2211). They are assigned each evaluation of `timelineScroll`: `revealBox.action = revealEnd` (ThreadTimeline.swift:321) and `revealBox.follow = followEnd` (:322). The box is `@State private var revealBox = TimelineRevealBox()` (:89) and goes into the environment at `.environment(\.revealTimelineEnd, revealBox)` (:393); `RevealTimelineEndKey.defaultValue` is nil (:2219). The two closures differ: `private func revealEnd() { guard !scrollState.showsJumpButton || tracking.isPinnedToBottom || tracking.distanceFromBottom < viewportHeight else { return }; followEnd() }` (ThreadTimeline.swift:787-790) and `private func followEnd() { tracking.isPinnedToBottom = true; anchorsBottomOnGrowth = true; position.scrollTo(edge: .bottom); noteScrollMovement() }` (:796-802). Callers, counted: `follow()` has exactly ONE call site, ThreadTimeline.swift:2089 (inside WorkingIndicator's expand button, inside `withAnimation(.snappy(duration: 0.24))`, only on the open transition). `action()` has exactly FOUR call sites, all in TimelineRows.swift: :1481 (WorkGroup un-collapse - note this call sits AFTER the closing brace of its `withAnimation(.snappy(duration: 0.24))`, i.e. OUTSIDE the animation), :1537 (WorkSteps 'show all', INSIDE `withAnimation(.snappy(duration: 0.24))`), :1708 (ToolRow inline-output expansion, `if expanded.wrappedValue { revealBox?.action() }` inside the animation), :2624 (TurnFinishedBlock expansion, `if isExpanded { revealBox?.action() }` inside the animation). R010 is correct; R012 is wrong.
resolutions.port_impact: SOURCE FACT. Two distinct reveal entry points. `action` must apply the three-way guard (jump button hidden OR pinned to bottom OR distanceFromBottom < viewportHeight) before revealing; `follow` must reveal unconditionally and also set pinned-to-bottom and bottom-anchored-on-growth. Wire the four row expansions to `action` and only the working-indicator chevron to `follow`. Keep WorkGroup's call outside its animation transaction and the other three inside theirs; that difference is observable as whether the scroll glide shares the row's animation.

resolutions.finding: G3. The (isMax, fastMode) -> TrackLook.Kind mapping is unstated.
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT. EffortSlider.swift:729-738: `private var look: TrackLook { let isMax = count > 1 && index == count - 1; let kind: TrackLook.Kind = switch (isMax, fastMode) { case (true, true): .fusion; case (true, false): .supercharged; case (false, true): .fast; case (false, false): .plain }; return TrackLook(kind: kind, brand: brand, pair: pair) }`. `TrackLook.Kind` has exactly FOUR cases, in declaration order: plain, supercharged, fast, fusion (EffortSlider.swift:969-976). Note `fastMode` reaching the slider is already `isFast = supportsFast && fastMode` from the card (EffortSlider.swift:541, passed at :632). Two further rules the mapping interacts with: a non-nil `pair` overrides the fill regardless of kind (`TrackLook.fill`, EffortSlider.swift:985-999, returns a LinearGradient of `[brand.fillColor] + pair.colors` before the switch is reached) and `TrackLook.effectIdentity` (:1024-1026) collapses a paired look to `.plain` so the fusion animation keeps its clock across kind changes. The animation frame rate also depends on kind: `TimelineView(.animation(minimumInterval: 1.0 / (kind == .supercharged && pair == nil ? 30 : 60), paused: paused))` (EffortSlider.swift:1050).
resolutions.port_impact: SOURCE FACT. Implement the exact 2x2 mapping; gate `isMax` on `count > 1` so a one-stop track never reads as maximum. Apply the pair gradient ahead of the kind's own fill, and drive supercharged-without-pair at 30 fps and everything else at 60.

Cursor stack: `NSCursor.openHand.push()` on grip hover-enter, `NSCursor.pop()` on hover-leave, both behind `guard !isDragged else { return }` after `isHoveringGrip = hovering` (:386-390); `NSCursor.closedHand.push()` once per drag, when `drag.id != id` (:233); `NSCursor.pop()` in `dragEnded()` behind `guard drag.id != nil` (:293-294); a compensating `NSCursor.pop()` in `.onChange(of: isDragged) { _, dragging in if !dragging, !isHoveringGrip { NSCursor.pop() } }` (:395-399); `.onDisappear { if isHoveringGrip { NSCursor.pop() }; isHoveringGrip = false }` (:391-394). `isDragged` is `drag.id == prompt.id` (:97), so the compensating pop only fires on the row that was actually dragged. Haptics: `.alignment` on a reorder move (:248), `.levelChange` on unlink (:258), `.alignment` on first pair-target acquisition (:279), `.levelChange` on bundling at drop (:290), `.levelChange` at :355. Release springs: `.spring(response: 0.36, dampingFraction: 0.78)` for the bundle (:286) and `.spring(response: 0.32, dampingFraction: 0.8)` for the settle (:297).

Windows has no NSCursor push/pop stack: model it as an explicit cursor-owner stack (a LIFO of cursor handles with SetCursor on top-of-stack) and mirror the same four push/pop sites so the balance rules survive; see the upstream defect noted separately for the row-removed-mid-drag leak.

resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT. Title: `title: git.activity ?? git.status?.branch ?? resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT. ChatView.swift:1139-1147: `if let thread = model.thread(runtime.threadID) { /* comment */ if model.settings.hydraEnabled, !thread.isHelper { HydraButton(thread: thread, runtime: runtime).transition(.softAppear) }; PermissionMenu(thread: thread) }`. resolutions.finding: G8. The minimap condition drops the `paneSize == .zero` case.
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT. ChatView.swift:108-109: `showsMinimap: !scene.dockedSides.contains(.leading) && (paneSize == .zero || paneSize.width - scene.reserve.leading - scene.reserve.trailing >= 900)`. The width test is on the pane width MINUS both leading and trailing reserves, not on the raw pane width, and the comparison is `>= 900` (not `>`). The `paneSize == .zero` disjunct means the rail is shown on the first frame, before the pane has been measured. The in-source rationale: the content column reads at up to 820 points and the rail floats over its gutter.
resolutions.port_impact: SOURCE FACT. Show the rail by default on the unmeasured first frame; hide it only once a real measurement comes back below the threshold, and subtract both docked-panel reserves before comparing to 900. A port that treats an unmeasured pane as zero width and hides the rail will flash the rail off then on.

resolutions.finding: G9. The changes-popover lifecycle in ComposerArea is entirely undescribed.
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT. `@State private var diffPopover = DiffPopoverCoordinator()` (ComposerView.swift:20). Its wiring, in source order on the inner VStack (ComposerView.swift:27-49): `VStack(alignment: .center, spacing: -ThreadChangesTab.overlap)` holding `TabSlot(runtime:diffPopover:showsChanges:)` and `ComposerView(...)`; `.background { AttachmentAnchorCapture { diffPopover.setFallbackAnchor($0) } }` (:32-34); `.background { if showsChanges { ChangeStatsRefresh(runtime: runtime) } }` (:35-38); `.onAppear { diffPopover.sync(isVisible: runtime.isDiffVisible, runtime: runtime) }` (:39); `.onChange(of: runtime.threadID) { diffPopover.sync(isVisible: runtime.isDiffVisible, runtime: runtime) }` (:41); `.onChange(of: runtime.isDiffVisible) { _, visible in diffPopover.sync(isVisible: visible, runtime: runtime) }` (:42-44); `.onChange(of: runtime.diffOpenRequest) { diffPopover.reopen(runtime: runtime) }` (:45-47); `.onDisappear { diffPopover.close() }` (:48); `.onChange(of: isColumnShown) { _, shown in if !shown { diffPopover.close() } }` (:49), where `@Environment(\.chatColumnIsShown) private var isColumnShown` (:5). The tab supplies the primary anchor: `ThreadChangesTab(stats: stats, anchor: { diffPopover.setAnchor($0) })` (ComposerView.swift:82-84). Area frame: `.frame(maxWidth: 820)`, `.padding(.horizontal, 20)`, `.padding(.bottom, 14)`, `.frame(maxWidth: .infinity)`, `.animation(Chrome.panelSlide, value: runtime.approvals.map(\.id))` (:52-56). Coordinator semantics (DiffInspector.swift:521-632): `popover.behavior = .semitransient`, `animates = true`, width 640, height 540 (:522-538); `sync` has three branches - different runtime (close, clear the old runtime's isDiffVisible, adopt, seed seenOpenRequest, and under a normal launch force the new runtime's isDiffVisible to false), first adoption (adopt, seed seenOpenRequest, and under a normal launch force isDiffVisible false and return), same runtime (set desiredVisible and show or close) (:551-570, with the capture guards at :557 and :563); `reopen` no-ops unless the runtime is the same one AND diffOpenRequest actually advanced past seenOpenRequest, then re-anchors without a close/open flash if the anchor is unchanged (:595-610); `resolvedAnchor()` prefers `runtime.diffAnchor` with `runtime.diffAnchorEdge`, else the tab anchor, else the fallback anchor, each only if `view.window != nil`, with edge `.maxY` (:615-625).
resolutions.port_impact: SOURCE FACT. The popover is owned by the composer area, not by the tab, and is driven by three runtime signals (threadID, isDiffVisible, diffOpenRequest) plus four lifecycle hooks (appear, disappear, column hidden, anchor arrival). Port the two-anchor arrangement: the tab's own rect when the changes tab is on screen, the composer area's rect when the follow-up queue has taken the tab's slot. Hiding the chat column must close the popover. 640x540 fixed.

resolutions.finding: G10. Which control does interrupt() vs takeBackRunningTurn() vs interruptAndSend() is unstated.
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT, three distinct controls. (a) The SEND BUTTON while running calls `runtime.interrupt()`: `Button { if isRunning { runtime.interrupt() } else { send() } }` (ComposerView.swift:829), glyph `Image(systemName: isRunning ? "stop.fill" : "arrow.up")` at `.frame(width: 28, height: 28)` in a circle, `.disabled(!isEnabled || runtime.isReverting)` with `isEnabled = isRunning || !draftEmpty`, accessibility label `isRunning ? "Stop" : (goesToHead ? "Send to a head" : "Send")` (:823-842). (b) ESCAPE calls `runtime.takeBackRunningTurn()`, but only as the first arm of a four-way chain: `case .escape: if runtime.isRunning { runtime.takeBackRunningTurn() } else if runtime.isTerminalVisible { runtime.isTerminalVisible = false } else if runtime.isDiffVisible { runtime.toggleDiff() } else { return false }` (ComposerView.swift:342-354). (c) RETURN while running calls `runtime.interruptAndSend()` via `send()`: `private func send() { guard !runtime.draft.isEmpty else { return }; historyIndex = nil; suggestions = SuggestionState(); if runtime.isRunning { runtime.interruptAndSend() } else { runtime.send() } }` (ComposerView.swift:370-383). The runtime behaviors differ materially. `takeBackRunningTurn()` (ThreadRuntime.swift:680-699+) only returns the words when `draft.isEmpty, !hasWorkingHeads, currentTurnID` resolves to a turn whose user item is a non-Hydra user message; otherwise it falls through to a bare `interrupt()`. On the happy path it interrupts, then polls `for _ in 0..<200 where phase != .idle { try? await Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(50)) }` (a 10-second ceiling) and only reverts if `phase == .idle, draft.isEmpty` and the turn is still present, with `restoreFiles: false`; on a revert failure it appends the notice "The stopped message was kept: \(error.localizedDescription)". `interruptAndSend()` (ThreadRuntime.swift:791-812) is guarded by `!isReverting, !draft.isEmpty, phase != .idle`, then tries `dispatchSentHead(text:attachments:)` first (clears the draft, no interrupt), then `if hasWorkingHeads { enqueueFollowUp(...); draft = ComposerDraft(); return }` (clears the draft, no interrupt), and only otherwise sets `pendingSend`, clears the draft and calls `interrupt()`. R015 was right that all three are called; it did not bind them to controls.
resolutions.port_impact: SOURCE FACT. Three different actions on one running turn, and the port must not merge them. Stop button = plain interrupt, turn stays in the thread. Escape = take back (stop + rewind the user message into the composer) with the four preconditions and the 10-second/200-poll watchdog, falling back to a plain interrupt whenever any precondition fails. Return = interrupt-and-send, which becomes queue-behind or dispatch-to-head whenever heads are working and never interrupts in those cases. Reproduce the notice string verbatim.

resolutions.finding: G11. Key precedence while the suggestion list is open is only half described.
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT. ComposerView.swift:312-330, the whole suggestion-open block, which runs BEFORE the ordinary switch: `if suggestions.isVisible { switch key { case .up: suggestions.selected = max(0, suggestions.selected - 1); return true; case .down: suggestions.selected = min(suggestions.items.count - 1, suggestions.selected + 1); return true; case .tab, .submit, .steer: pick(suggestions.items[suggestions.selected]); return true; case .escape: dismissedSuggestions = true; suggestions = SuggestionState(); return true; case .deleteAtStart: return false } }`. Six `ComposerKey` cases, all handled: up, down, tab, submit, steer, escape, deleteAtStart (tab/submit/steer share one arm, so five arms). Only `.deleteAtStart` returns false and falls through to the text view. Outside the suggestion block the same keys mean different things (ComposerView.swift:331-366): `.submit` -> send(), `.steer` -> steer(), `.up`/`.down` -> `recall(older:)` history recall, `.tab` -> return false, `.escape` -> the four-way chain in G10, `.deleteAtStart` -> drop `runtime.draft.command` then the last of `runtime.draft.quotes`, each inside `withAnimation(Chrome.panelSlide)`, else return false.
resolutions.port_impact: SOURCE FACT. While the suggestion list is open, Tab, Return AND Cmd-Return all commit the highlighted item; arrows move the clamped selection; Escape dismisses and latches `dismissedSuggestions` so the list does not immediately reopen; backspace-at-start alone falls through. Arrow-key history recall must be suppressed while the list is open. Note `pick(suggestions.items[suggestions.selected])` is an unguarded subscript - see upstream defects.

resolutions.finding: G12. The rewindable rule that decides whether revert/edit controls exist at all is unreported.

resolutions.port_impact: SOURCE FACT + ENGINEERING DECISION. Do not collapse these into one helper. The port needs (i) a fixed-content popover primitive that pre-measures once, clips top-aligned and never republishes its size - used by the badge, link, head-hover, attachment and diff popovers; (ii) a live-resizing popover for the prompt editor; (iii) a caret-anchored, focus-preserving suggestion panel sized 340 wide by min(340, 44 + max(n,1)*26); (iv) a dismissal policy per site: Escape+outside-click monitors for badge/prompt-editor/attachment/diff, Escape only for the link popover, and hover-driven only for the head-hover card. On Windows, substitute the NSEvent local monitors with a message filter or a top-level hook scoped to the app's own threads (they are LOCAL monitors - they never see other applications' events).

resolutions.finding: X8. macOS primitives with no Windows equivalent, needing one substitution strategy each.
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT, corrected census. (a) NSCursor push/pop: TimelineMinimap.swift:218 (`NSCursor.pointingHand.push()`) and :252 (`NSCursor.pop()`); ProseRunView.swift:35, :51, :57; MarkdownView.swift InlineText's hover (same shape); FollowUpQueueTab.swift:233, :294, :389, :392, :398. (b) CADisplayLink: exactly two, and the frame-rate claim is WRONG for one of them. `VeilClock` uses `NSScreen.main.displayLink(target:selector:)` and IS the only site that sets `link.preferredFrameRateRange = CAFrameRateRange(minimum: 24, maximum: 60, preferred: 30)` (StreamVeil.swift:174-180); `LinkTextVeil` uses `view.displayLink(target:selector:)` and sets NO frame-rate range at all (StreamVeil.swift:347, :358-360). A repo-wide grep for `preferredFrameRateRange` returns exactly one hit. VeilClock additionally skips its tick entirely while `ScrollActivity.shared.isScrolling` (StreamVeil.swift:184-186) and invalidates itself once past its deadline. (c) CAReplicatorLayer: the type appears at exactly two lines, both in one class - `private let rows = CAReplicatorLayer()` and `private let columns = CAReplicatorLayer()` in `DotFieldLayerView` (ComposerWorkingDots.swift:57-58). The critic's attribution to 'ComposerWorkingDots, ChatBadge's attention overlay and HydraDelegationBlock's sweep' is right in substance but wrong in type: those three are all SwiftUI wrappers over the same `DotFieldLayerView.Representable` - ComposerWorkingDots.swift:16, ChatBadge.swift:58, and `DotFieldSweep` (ComposerWorkingDots.swift:25-35) which is used at HydraPanel.swift:75 and at TimelineRows.swift:703 inside `HydraDelegationBlock`. Its literals: dotSize 2, pitch 8, maxRows 3, period 2.2, columnDelay 0.045, rowDelay 0.09, animationKey "pulse", sweepPeriod 0.8, sweepColumnDelay 0.022 (ComposerWorkingDots.swift:68-80). Both DotFieldSweep and ComposerWorkingDots honour `accessibilityReduceMotion` (DotFieldSweep draws nothing at all; ComposerWorkingDots passes `animated: !reduceMotion`). (d) CASpringAnimation mass 1 / stiffness 170 / damping 26 with `animation.duration = animation.settlingDuration`: exactly one site, AttachmentFlight.swift:92-104, applied to three key paths in order - "bounds.size", "position", "cornerRadius" (:106-110). (e) NSHapticFeedbackManager: eight call sites, five of them in this family - EffortSlider.swift:812 (.alignment, drag stop), FollowUpQueueTab.swift:248 (.alignment), :258 (.levelChange), :279 (.alignment), :290 (.levelChange), :355 (.levelChange); the other three are outside the family (ModelsSettingsPage.swift:123, ShortcutsSettingsPage.swift:484-485, SidebarView.swift:799). (f) TextKit duality, verified: `ComposerNSTextView` overrides `draw(_:)` for its placeholder (ComposerTextView.swift:198), and the source records that AppKit answers any draw override by falling back to TextKit 1, so `updateHeight()` measures through TextKit 2 first and TextKit 1 second - `var contentHeight: CGFloat = 18; if let layoutManager = textView.textLayoutManager { layoutManager.ensureLayout(for: layoutManager.documentRange); contentHeight = layoutManager.usageBoundsForTextContainer.height } else if let layoutManager = textView.layoutManager, let container = textView.textContainer { layoutManager.ensureLayout(for: container); contentHeight = layoutManager.usedRect(for: container).height }` (ComposerTextView.swift:360-373), then `let total = ceil(max(18, contentHeight) + textView.textContainerInset.height * 2)` applied only when `abs(parent.height - total) > 0.5` (:374-375), the whole thing guarded by `textView.bounds.width > 24` (:361). Without the TextKit 1 arm the pill never grew past one line. LinkTextView builds its own `NSTextStorage` + `NSLayoutManager` + `NSTextContainer` in `init()` with `lineFragmentPadding = 0`, and the source records why (a bare container handed to `init(frame:textContainer:)` is held weakly and released, leaving every link paragraph blank) - LinkParagraphView.swift:292-306.
resolutions.port_impact: SOURCE FACT + ENGINEERING DECISION. Per primitive: (a) an explicit LIFO cursor-owner stack with SetCursor at the top, mirroring each push/pop site one-for-one; (b) a composition-timer abstraction - the veil clock throttled to ~30 fps and paused during scrolling, the AppKit veil left at the compositor's rate; (c) a single replicated-dot-field control with the nine literals above, used in three places, drawing nothing under reduced motion; (d) a critically-damped spring integrator (m=1, k=170, c=26) run to its settling time over size, position and corner radius together; (e) haptics have no Windows equivalent - drop them silently, do not substitute sound; (f) one text-layout stack that owns its storage explicitly.

resolutions.finding: X9. Three caches key on whole message text and must be sized together.
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT, every figure verified. `MarkdownView.blockCache = RecentCache<String, [MarkdownBlock]>(limit: 800)` (MarkdownView.swift:107); `RichLink.prettyCache = RecentCache<String, AttributedString>(limit: 1200)` (MarkdownView.swift:563); `TableBlock.cellCache = RecentCache<String, AttributedString>(limit: 1200)` (MarkdownView.swift:1348). Fixed rings: `MarkdownView.streamingSlots = 48` over `streamingParses: [(text: String, parse: MarkdownParser.Parse)]`, evicting with `removeFirst()` when full (MarkdownView.swift:115, :130); `RichLink.streamingSlots = 4` over `streamingPretty` (MarkdownView.swift:568, :575). Other caches in the family: `TimelineBlockCache` keeps at most 24 threads in an explicit LRU (`while order.count > 24 { ... }`, ThreadTimeline.swift:1650-1653); `TimelineMinimap.entryCache = RecentCache<String, TimelineMinimapEntry>(limit: 400)` (TimelineMinimap.swift:39); `DiffDetailCache.cache = RecentCache<String, DiffFile>(limit: 60)` (TimelineRows.swift:2185); `HydraDelegationBlock.readingCache = RecentCache<String, HydraPrompts.StreamedDelegations>(limit: 200)` (TimelineRows.swift:776); `FileIndex.built = RecentCache<String, (entries: [Entry], builtAt: Date)>(limit: 2)` with `freshness: TimeInterval = 60` (ComposerView.swift:1125, :1127). Wholesale flushes, not LRU: `FaviconCache.memory` is a plain dictionary flushed entirely at 300 - `if memory.count >= 300 { memory.removeAll(keepingCapacity: true) }; memory[key] = image` (MarkdownView.swift:931-932); `LinkTitles.Store.titles` likewise at 400 - `if titles.count >= 400 { titles.removeAll(keepingCapacity: true) }; titles[id] = title` (LinkTitles.swift:106-107), while `claimed` is only ever inserted into (:98, :109) and never cleared. Also in the family: `ThreadRuntime.turnDiffs` limit 64 and `revisionDiffs` limit 4 (ThreadRuntime.swift:1920-1921), the latter recreated wholesale on every `diffRevision` change (:194-197).
resolutions.port_impact: SOURCE FACT. Port the exact limits; they are tuned against each other (the source comment on streamingSlots records that four slots caused twenty heads to evict each other's parse on every flush). Reproduce the two wholesale flushes as flushes, not as LRU eviction - the 301st favicon really does drop all 300. See upstream_defects for the LinkTitles `claimed` consequence.

resolutions.finding: X10. Every editable surface keeps its edit state on ThreadRuntime rather than in the view.
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT. Three properties on ThreadRuntime: `var followUpEdit: PromptEdit?` (ThreadRuntime.swift:216), `var followUpsCollapsed = false` (:220), `var messageEdit: PromptEdit?` (:228). Each has an explicit lifetime rule in a didSet on the collection it shadows: `turns` didSet clears `messageEdit` when its turn leaves (`if let edit = messageEdit, !turns.contains(where: { $0.id == edit.id }) { messageEdit = nil }`, :176) and also drops that turn's cached diff (:177-180); `followUps` didSet clears `followUpEdit` the same way (didSet :207-211, the clear at :209). Consumers: messageEdit is read as `let isEditing = entry.turnID != nil && runtime.messageEdit?.id == entry.turnID` (TimelineRows.swift:87), toggled by the pencil (:134), synced into the editor popover by `editor.sync(isEditing ? runtime.messageEdit : nil, dismiss: { runtime.messageEdit = nil })` (:209), and cleared by MessageEditor.swift:165 and :174. followUpEdit is read as `let isEditing = runtime.followUpEdit?.id == prompt.id` (FollowUpQueueTab.swift:342), toggled at :457, synced at :511, cleared by FollowUpEditor.swift:30 and :34. followUpsCollapsed is read as `private var isCollapsed: Bool { runtime.followUpsCollapsed }` (FollowUpQueueTab.swift:31) and toggled inside `withAnimation(Chrome.panelSlide)` at :53. All three also gate idle detection: `&& draft.isEmpty && followUpEdit == nil && messageEdit == nil` (ThreadRuntime.swift:3515).
resolutions.port_impact: SOURCE FACT. Hold all three on the per-thread runtime object, not in row state. Scrolling a row out of a virtualized list, or leaving and re-entering the thread, must leave the editor open exactly where it was; and the thread must not be treated as idle while any editor is open or the draft is non-empty. Clear each edit automatically when the turn or follow-up it points at disappears.

upstream_defects: LinkTitles.swift:98-109 - the `claimed` set is inserted into on claim (:98) and again on finish (:109) and is NEVER cleared, while `titles` is flushed wholesale at 400 entries (:106). After a flush, any video id that was already claimed can never be claimed again (`claimed.insert(id).inserted` returns false), so its title is permanently unavailable for the rest of the launch even though the cache that held it is empty. `finish` also inserts into `claimed` when `title` is nil, so a failed fetch is never retried either. Reproduce, do not fix.

MarkdownView.swift:931-932 (FaviconCache.memory) and LinkTitles.swift:106 (titles) - both are dictionaries flushed with `removeAll(keepingCapacity: true)` the moment they reach 300 / 400, so a single insertion past the threshold discards every cached favicon / title rather than evicting one. Observable as every favicon in a long thread blanking and re-fetching at once. Reproduce.

ComposerView.swift:320-322 - `case .tab, .submit, .steer: pick(suggestions.items[suggestions.selected])` subscripts `items` with `selected` under no bounds check. `selected` is clamped only in the `.up`/`.down` arms (:315, :318), and `min(suggestions.items.count - 1, ...)` yields -1 for an empty list. If `suggestions.isVisible` were ever true with an empty `items`, this traps. Port with the same lack of a guard's *behavior* but do not crash: the Windows port should treat the out-of-range case as a no-op, which is the closest non-crashing equivalent.

AttachmentFlight.swift:55-59 - the reduce-motion guard returns BEFORE the `if let existing = window { existing.orderOut(nil); window = nil }` teardown. If reduced motion is turned on while a flight is in the air, the in-flight ghost window is never ordered out by a subsequent call; it is only removed by its own CATransaction completion block. Narrow, but reproduce the ordering.

AttachmentFlight.swift:195-203 - `AttachmentDrops.shared.take()` consumes the armed drop before `fly(...)` is called, and `fly` then returns without animating under reduced motion or on a nil cgImage / nil NSScreen.main. The drop is silently lost. Harmless as shipped because the only call site passes no completion and the chip is drawn by layout regardless, but it is the source's behavior and must not be 'fixed' by deferring `take()`.

FollowUpQueueTab.swift:156-164 vs :386-399 - cursor-stack leak when a queued follow-up is removed mid-drag. `onChange(of: runtime.followUps.map(\.id))` calls `dragEnded()` (:159), which pops the closedHand (:294). The openHand pushed on grip hover (:389) is popped only by hover-leave (which is suppressed during a drag by `guard !isDragged`, :388), by `.onChange(of: isDragged)` when the row is released away from the grip (:398), or by `.onDisappear` when `isHoveringGrip` is still true (:392). A row deleted or sent while dragged with the pointer off the grip satisfies none of these, leaving one unbalanced NSCursor push for the rest of the launch. Reproduce the structure; a Windows cursor-owner stack should mirror the same push/pop sites rather than silently balancing itself.

ThreadRuntime.swift:206 - `private(set) var followUps: [FollowUpPrompt] = []` is indented four spaces deeper than its siblings. Cosmetic only; noted so a port's diff reviewer does not read it as a nesting change.

WebsiteCaptures.swift:857 and :861 (and everything reachable only from WebsiteCaptures/TourCaptures) - gated on `WebsiteCaptures.isEnabled`, which is `CaptureRun.isEnabled` (WebsiteCaptures.swift:26), which is `outputDirectory != nil` (CaptureRun.swift:27), which is non-nil only when the process was launched with `--website-captures <dir>` or `--tour-captures <dir>` (CaptureRun.swift:10-19). These are launch arguments for the marketing-capture build, never present in a normal launch, and the run also swaps in its own UserDefaults suite "iordv.droppycode.website-captures" (CaptureRun.swift:40) and its own storage root. The port does not need this subsystem.

DiffInspector.swift:557 and :563 - the two `!WebsiteCaptures.isEnabled` conjuncts inside DiffPopoverCoordinator.sync. Under every normal launch `WebsiteCaptures.isEnabled` is false, so both conditions reduce to their left operand: adopting a runtime (or switching to one) always forces `runtime.isDiffVisible = false`, i.e. the changes popover never restores itself open when the composer first appears or moves to another thread. The capture-run branch that would preserve an already-open diff is unreachable outside a capture launch. The port must implement the normal-launch behavior (always close on adopt/switch) and may omit the flag entirely.
